title: The Communist Manifesto
author: Karl Marx
Friedrich Engels
edition_analyzed: Original German edition; standard 20th-century English translations
target_audience: Students of political science, history, and philosophy
General readers interested in socialism, communism, or revolutionary movements
Scholars examining the development of leftist thought
core_themes: The role and power of the working class (proletariat)
Critique of capitalism and bourgeois society
Vision for a classless, communist society
primary_purpose: To succinctly explain the aims of the Communist League and present the principles of communism—calling for the working class to unite and overthrow capitalist structures to establish a classless society.

structure_format.organization: Four sections: (1) Bourgeois and Proletarians (historical materialism & class struggle), (2) Proletarians and Communists (role of party, core tenets), (3) Socialist and Communist Literature (critiques rivals), (4) Position of Communists in Relation to the Various Existing Opposition Parties
features: Political rhetoric and calls to action
Manifesto-style closing ('Workers of the world, unite!')

key_concepts_lessons: All historical developments stem from struggles between social classes.
Bourgeois capitalism creates and exacerbates social and economic inequality.
The working class (proletariat) is inherently pitted against the owning class (bourgeoisie) and will eventually be forced to revolt against exploitation.
Communists advocate for the abolition of bourgeois property, private ownership of the means of production, and the establishment of a classless society.
) is central to successful revolutionary change.
notable_features: Analysis of other contemporary socialist strands
Famous concluding line: 'Workers of the world, unite!'
cultural_historical_context: Written during a period of political turmoil across Europe, on the eve of the 1848 revolutions. It responded to rising industrial capitalism, widespread social inequality, and the emergence of the workers' movement. The Manifesto became one of the most influential political documents in modern history.
reception_impact: Profound influence on the development of communist and socialist thought
Foundation for Marxist theory and later revolutionary movements around the world
Repeatedly banned or censored in various countries due to its revolutionary message
Studied in universities and by political activists globally
Central text in labor, anti-capitalist, and leftist movements for over 170 years
comparable_titles: Socialism: Utopian and Scientific by Friedrich Engels
The State and Revolution by Vladimir Lenin
The Road to Serfdom by F.A. Hayek (as a counterpoint)
